source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Corvette Body, p.1B-22

procedures.title: Leather and coated fabrics: clean
steps: Work up a thick suds on gauze or cheesecloth and apply it to the surface.
Repeat with just a damp cloth, no soap.
Dry the surface with a soft cloth.
notes: Never use body polishes or cleaners, volatile cleaners, furniture polish, oils, varnishes, or household cleaning or bleaching agents.

procedures.title: Carpet: clean
steps: Brush or vacuum the carpet thoroughly; often nothing more is needed.
If very dirty, take the carpet out of the car and vacuum it well.
Clean about 1 square foot at a time with a foaming upholstery cleaner.
After each area, vacuum up as much cleaner as possible.
Fluff the pile with an air hose, then let the carpet dry.
Once fully dry, fluff the pile again with the air hose.
notes: A lightly soiled carpet can be cleaned in the car with a little foaming upholstery cleaner and a brush.

procedures.title: Carpets and covers: remove and cement
steps: To remove front compartment carpet, take off the sill plates and loosen the console trim (see Front End - Cowl Area and Console Trim).
Where carpet is cemented: strip off all old carpet, jute, etc. left stuck to the floor.
Make sure the floor is fairly clean and dry.
Apply 3M-1711 cement or equivalent per the package directions.

procedures.title: Seats: remove and adjust
steps: Removal: Remove the bolt holding each front support to the floor.
Fold the seat back forward.
Loosen the 2 bolts on each seat hold-down bracket.
Slide the seat forward out of the brackets.
Adjustment: Set seat height, front and rear, with shims or washers.
Change backrest angle by adjusting the stops on the lower edge of the seat back.

procedures.title: Body mounting bolts: check torque
steps: Periodically check torque on all body mount bolts to help prevent squeaks and rattles.
Torque all bolts shown in figure 49 in the manual to spec.
notes: Figure 49 in the manual shows the underbody-to-frame mounting brackets.
Shims on the rear crossmember are cemented in place.

procedures.title: Body repairs: general instructions
steps: When welding steel parts mounted on the body, keep flame and weld heat off the plastic panels.
Shield the surrounding area with wet asbestos or similar; several layers of aluminum foil work well if clear of direct flame.
Straighten steel parts in the body carefully; when using hydraulic jacks or similar, make sure the part bracing the fixed end can take the load.
If alignment is off after collision or other damage, inspect the steel reinforcements in the cowl and sill areas carefully.
Follow the path of the impact force and check the body for broken bonds and cracks before, during and after repair.
notes: Fiberglass parts are tougher than steel but will not yield or take a set, so they cannot be straightened.
Small cracks and bond faults usually grow if not repaired.
